correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the singleton optimum \(\sec(\pi/(2m))\) by an explicit nonnegative polynomial and a global Chebyshev supporting-line argument, identifies exactly two contacts, then uses those contacts to prove the odd-multiple upper bound and an explicit contact-positive perturbation to prove strict improvement otherwise. Quantifiers and boundary assumptions are \(m\ge3\), \(n\ge2\), \(n\ne m\), with real coefficients and full-circle nonnegativity. The bundled finite checker only corroborates the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The direct support-restricted Carathéodory–Fejér sources contain the problem framework but the inspected material does not state the complete criterion \(n\equiv m\pmod{2m}\). A related three-character Sidon secant theorem solves a different norm problem, and the closest exact support computations cover isolated frequency sets rather than all \((m,n)\). Statement-level implication comparisons therefore leave the final claim uncovered, subject to the recorded historical-literature risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent resonance theorem may exist in older cosine-polynomial or positive-definite-sequence literature under notation not captured by the checked aliases.

The theorem classifies equality versus strict improvement but does not identify the strict-regime optimum, so it should not be read as dominating exact-value results for particular nonresonant supports.

value.rationale: The final claim gives a natural complete boundary theorem for one-frequency augmentation of the singleton Carathéodory–Fejér problem: every distinct auxiliary frequency is classified, the equality class is an explicit arithmetic progression, and the mechanism is geometric contact annihilation. It is reusable structural information rather than a table entry, routine substitution, or unsupported significance claim.
